subject: Culture
title: Chaperone Traditions
description: Learn Chaperone Traditions in one minute.

hook.text: In Victorian England an unmarried woman couldn't walk with a man without a chaperone—even her fiancé.

buildup.text: Chaperone systems existed to guarantee female virtue through constant surveillance by older relatives.

discovery.text: In Latin America the 'dueña' tradition lasted well into the 20th century. Dates required a family witness.

twist.text: The chaperone protected the family's honor, not the woman's safety. The threat was gossip, not danger.

climax.text: Dating apps eliminated the chaperone—and transferred trust from families to platform algorithms.

punchline.text: The chaperone was the first trust algorithm.

quiz.question: What was the Latin American term for a female chaperone?
